| [CASE-044](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-044.md) | The thermostat: Dennett's knife edge between agent and device | An ordinary thermostat holding a room at a setpoint. Dennett calls it the simplest artifact that can sustain the intentional stance, and Orseau et al. place it "on the knife edge": "if temperature is below the command, start heating" and "make sure the temperature is close to the command" are descriptions of comparable simplicity. It is the permissiveness objection's standard case, here given a code at its second appearance after [CLAIM-010](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-010.md). | Active |
| [CASE-045](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-045.md) v4 | Measuring the dancing couple: is the pair a nearly decomposable block during the dance and not after it? | A proposed study, not run. Motion-capture several couples dancing an improvised partner dance to recorded music, and record the same people standing and talking after the song. Fit a linear model to the joint kinematics, with the music's beat as an exogenous input. Then ask whether the pair is a block whose gap beats its Occam factor during the dance and not after, whether it compensates under a perturbation, and whether the coupling runs both ways. | Active |
| [CASE-046](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-046.md) v2 | A partner-dancing couple, lindy hop, tango or salsa, while they dance | The owner's case (2026-10-11). Two social dancers improvise together. | [CASE-137](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-137.md) v2 | Clive Wearing: a musician left by encephalitis with almost no memory of his past and none of the last minutes, who still plays, sight-reads and conducts, keeps his attachment to his wife, and writes over and over that he has just become conscious for the first time | The owner's case, proposed at U26 of the exchange of 2026-10-22 ("if we haven't already examined the case of Clive Wearing, that might be another good addition"). The record had no amnesia case. It separates skill and short-horizon organization, which persist, from autobiographical continuity and experienced ownership of one's past, which do not. Not shown by it: that the unity of his present experience is an illusion, or that his denials of past consciousness are evidence of its absence. | Active |
| [CASE-139](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-139.md) | Chinese martial traditions through the Cultural Revolution: practices restricted, teachers persecuted and teaching driven underground, then after 1978 a reconstruction of Shaolin martial arts through heritage policy and tourism in which local practitioners and authorized institutions dispute who carries the tradition | The owner's case at U37 of the branch of the exchange of 2026-10-22: the "(various) perspectival interruption(s) caused by the Chinese Cultural Revolution", near the record's martial-arts material ([CASE-130](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-130.md)). A case family, not one example: skills that survived in bodies while teaching became dangerous; practices that persisted under a different organization of authority; survival in marginal carriers; and a reconstruction that became a source of authenticity. Not shown: what was continuous and what was rebuilt, which is the question it raises. | Active |
| [CASE-140](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-140.md) | The attributed self: two people with similar dispositions hear the same negative characterization, one told it comes from a few critics and the other believing it speaks for nearly everyone who matters to them, so that the words are fixed and only their attributed breadth differs | A39's proposed test of the imagined audience, in the exchange of 2026-10-22, filed at the owner's request. It holds the content of a judgement fixed and varies only the social authority the hearer attributes to it. A39: "These cases distinguish the content of a judgment from the social authority attributed to it." As stipulated it predicts nothing; run with real people, it would test [CLAIM-415](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-415.md). | Active |
| [CASE-141](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-141.md) | The label that confirms itself: a pupil wrongly labelled disruptive is watched more closely, ordinary conduct is read as misconduct, the pupil's frustration produces real misconduct, and the label looks justified in hindsight | A39's second reading of "I am whatever you say I am", in the exchange of 2026-10-22, filed at the owner's request with its variant [CASE-142](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-142.md). An attribution can produce the conduct that later seems to justify it, through the institution's response to the attribution, not through the pupil's coming to believe it. Not shown: how often labels work this way; A39: "That's a possible self-fulfilling process, not a universal consequence of stigmatizing labels." | Active |
| [CASE-142](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-142.md) | The label confirmed by resistance: a critic calls someone hostile, the person answers the characterization angrily, and the critic cites the anger as proof, so the judgement is confirmed by the response of someone who rejects it | A39's third reading of "I am whatever you say I am", in the exchange of 2026-10-22, filed at the owner's request as a variant of [CASE-141](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-141.md). What differs is the route: the judgement is rejected, not absorbed, and the rejection is what confirms it. A39: "Here an interpretive regime partially manufactures the evidence it uses to justify itself." Not shown: that resistance always confirms; the person can also answer the judgement without the answer being read as evidence for it. | Active |
| [CASE-143](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-143.md) | Franklin's borrowed book: Benjamin Franklin, opposed by a new member of the Pennsylvania Assembly when he stood again as its clerk, asked to borrow a rare book from him rather than courting him, returned it with thanks, and found the man civil and later a friend | The owner's U1 of the exchange of 2026-10-22, "Ben Franklin Effect Explained", read at U2 as a "perspectival invitation". Documented in Franklin's Autobiography ([LIT-1402](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1402.md); the passage was read in the Project Gutenberg text on 2026-10-23), and the origin of the "Ben Franklin effect", that doing someone a favour can increase liking for them, tested by Jecker and Landy ([LIT-1419](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1419.md)). The standing is the anecdote's, as Franklin told it; the reading is the exchange's. | Active |
| [CASE-144](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-144.md) v2 | The evaluator that stops tracking: two populations of specialists with identical capabilities and task streams, one scored against independent outcomes and one by an evaluator that weights evidence agreeing with its previously favoured specialists, after a shift that makes a marginalized specialist uniquely competent | Proposed in the exchange of 2026-10-23, "Framework Overview Request", at A5 (section 5) with A4's "corrigibility trap", after the owner asked which experiments could "kill multiple birds with one stone" (U4) and which questions simulation could answer (U5). One design bears on [CASE-092](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-092.md), [CASE-108](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-108.md) and [CASE-117](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-117.md) at once, and separates four causes of a failure to adapt. A5's central question: "Under what conditions does an organization become unable to recognize or act upon evidence that its own organization of interpretation and authority has rendered inconsequential?" Not run. | Active |
| [CASE-145](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-145.md) | Perspective without collective agency: populations given the same structured norms, categories or interpretive training, some interacting and some acquiring similar dispositions independently, with and without any mechanism for collective decision or coordinated intervention | Proposed at A4 of the exchange of 2026-10-23, "Framework Overview Request", which called it "the most philosophically important new experiment". It asks whether a distributed organizational perspective can be identified without attributing a further collective agent, [CLAIM-418](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-418.md)'s separation tested, and bears on [QUESTION-260](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-260.md). A4's condition: it helps only if it says in advance what distinguishes a shared perspective from correlated responses or learned norms. Not run. | Active |
| [CASE-146](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-146.md) | Two friendships across a group line: in one, the friend becomes an exception and the person's view of the friend's group is unchanged; in the other, what happens with the friend changes how the person takes other members of the group, though the friendships are alike in warmth and in what each learns | From the exchange of 2026-10-22, "Ben Franklin Effect Explained", A4 and A5, on the owner's U4 about intergroup contact. A4: "A prejudiced person can befriend a member of a targeted group while preserving their prejudice toward everyone else. They simply classify the friend as an exception." A5 drew the two outcomes as "Exception formation" and "Category reorganization". Held fixed: the friendship and its favourable information. Varied: whether the friend's conduct is allowed to bear on the category. | Active |
| [CASE-147](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-147.md) | Conversation against argument: in Kalla and Broockman's field experiments, canvassers who exchanged personal narratives nonjudgmentally reduced exclusionary attitudes durably, while arguments alone did not produce comparable effects | Cited at A4 of the exchange of 2026-10-22, "Ben Franklin Effect Explained", as "suggestive evidence" for the prediction that cooperative enactment changes attitudes more durably than information. Kalla and Broockman (2020, [LIT-1407](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1407.md)), registered unread; the description is the exchange's and the abstract's, unchecked against the paper. The standing is the study's, not the reading's. | Active |
| [CASE-148](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-148.md) | Perspective transplantation: two populations matched in behaviour exchange different combinations of learned interpretive rules, specialist parameters, training histories, institutional rules and shared memory, and are then set where the transferred parts disagree with their new surroundings | Proposed at A4 of the exchange of 2026-10-23, "Framework Overview Request", as an extension of [CASE-101](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-101.md). It asks which components carry a perspective's characteristic organization when it moves between carriers: [CLAIM-417](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-417.md)'s realization, character and lineage, tested by transfer. A4: "No transfer experiment can settle numerical identity merely by demonstrating causal continuity." Not run. | Active |
| [CASE-149](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-149.md) | Dancing to the same or different music, seen or unseen: in dyads facing each other, shared music and visual contact were removed independently, and each synchronized different movements of the pair | Bigand et al. (2024), [LIT-1424](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1424.md), read in [NOTE-1093](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1093.md). Filed from the owner's exchange "Framework Overview Request" of 2026-10-23 as an external result meeting part of the aim of the proposed study [CASE-045](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-045.md). In 35 dyads, shared music and visual contact were varied in a 2 × 2 design; each raised synchrony in different movement components, with no interaction, and the timing of the synchrony could not tell the two apart. Not shown: the direction of coupling, a perturbation response, or anything about trained partner dancing with touch. | Active |
| [CASE-150](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-150.md) | Economic alignment and political alignment: Kleinman, Liu and Redding find, using China's integration into the world economy and falling air-transport costs as sources of variation, that countries whose welfare becomes more dependent on each other's productivity become more politically aligned | Cited at A6 of the exchange of 2026-10-22, "Ben Franklin Effect Explained", after the owner's U6 on trade and peace, as "a paper that makes the connection almost literally". Kleinman, Liu and Redding (2024, [LIT-1416](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1416.md)), registered unread; the description is the exchange's and the abstract's. The standing is the study's, not the reading's. | Active |
| [CASE-153](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-153.md) v2 | The self-protecting sentry: a hidden world, safe or dangerous, a sentry process that favours sheltering and can block inspection with weight κg, an investigator that favours inspecting, which reveals the state with 90% accuracy at a small cost; train in danger, switch to safety, and compare a Bayesian baseline, a habit baseline, the learned-authority model, an independent audit and a protected investigator, then cross governance feedback, evidence restriction and correction rights in a 2×2×2 design | Proposed in the exchange of 2026-10-23 (workbench entry of 2026-10-24, U17), after the owner asked to "brainstorm some minimal toy models we could apply to simulate our abstraction for experiments. there may also be some readily available options that fit our constraints already." The smallest model of the protective lock-in in [CLAIM-446](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-446.md), built on [CASE-092](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-092.md) and [CASE-099](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-099.md). At U18 the owner pointed to [CASE-124](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-124.md) as the better core, and the exchange moved there ([CASE-156](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-156.md)). Not run. | Active |
| [CASE-154](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-154.md) | One representation, two tasks, one bounded observer: with X₁, X₂ independent fair bits and an observer that reads one coordinate and cannot compute XOR, the raw pair U = (X₁, X₂) gives error 50% on Q_A = X₁ ⊕ X₂ and 0% on Q_B = X₁, and the compressed V = X₁ ⊕ X₂ gives 0% and 50%; a legibility regime can enable one perspective's distinction while disabling another's, with no task-independent sense in which it is better | From the exchange of 2026-10-24 (workbench entry of 2026-10-24, U22), after the owner said "let's work on those connections": a deduction from [CLAIM-199](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-199.md)'s XOR example, checked when filed. It ties bounded legibility to competing concerns: a representation that serves one task can destroy another's for the same observer, so a failure of one perspective under a legibility regime may be a resource limit and not an exclusion. | Active |
| [CASE-155](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-155.md) v3 | Authority as a replicator population: for a distribution π of control over processes with mean qualities q, the expected Maynard-Cross update is π_a q_a / v, Bayes' rule when q is each process's likelihood; the Maynard dynamic is the Taylor dynamic slowed by 1/v, so the two share their orbits; mean quality climbs at the rate Var_π(q); and when a process's score rises with its own share, ℓ′ = ℓ + h + c(2π − 1) has an unstable threshold π* = (1 − h/c)/2, above which a process the evidence disfavours captures the organization | Filed at the owner's direction, 2026-10-24, after asking whether the tools of Soma et al. ([THEORY-899](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-899.md)) or related work could formalize the record's abstract governance dynamics. Four results, each checked when filed, two by script. It reads authority as the population vector of a replicator dynamic. Evidence-tracking authority is then Bayesian, and authority-dependent scoring gives lock-in with an explicit correction threshold. | Active |
| [CASE-156](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-156.md) v2 | A legibility filter as the ν of the meaning–authority–legibility model: in a safe world where 15% of raw cues are alarms, an admission rule P(admit \| y, r) = σ(c + χry) with c = 0 and χr = 2 admits 88.1% of alarms and 11.9% of reassurances, so 56.6% of the admitted record is alarms with the world and the sensors unchanged; at symmetry the mean admitted evidence is χσ′(c)r to first order, so ν = η_m χ σ′(c); and r_t = λᵗr₀ + ε Σ λ^(t−1−j) a_j is an exponentially weighted history of authority | From the exchange of 2026-10-24 (workbench entry of 2026-10-24, U18–U19). The owner: "i think we already have a three variable system somewhere, where the third component is described as legibility", then "flesh this out further". A microfoundation for one of [CASE-124](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-124.md)'s abstract couplings: selective admission of evidence, checked when filed. It gives r an observational semantics and reads r as the memory of past authority. Selection-aware inference is the control that the pathology has to beat. | Active |
| [CASE-157](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-157.md) v2 | Boosting the vote: in the owner's 2014 model, voters of fixed accuracy drawn from Beta(2, 2) vote in a weight-averaged election, and every voter's weight is multiplied by 1 + f when their own vote was right and 1 − f when not, with a fraction replaced each round at weight 1; with full-information feedback the weighted result rises from 0.50 toward 0.98 as f grows, and churn only costs in a world that never changes; the model escapes the hive mind's absorbing states because every voter is scored, heeded or not, and it assumes away the capture its author predicted | Filed at the owner's direction, 2026-10-24, after the owner suggested taking inspiration from the experiments in dmarx/BoostTheVote. A thought-experiment written in R in 2014, read at commit b5bca8f and re-run here through a Python port (scratch/formal/boost_the_vote.py). It is the full-information counterpart of the replicator construction. What it shows, what it assumes, and the three-axis extension it suggests are recorded, and the extension was run on 2026-10-25. | Active |
| [CASE-158](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-158.md) v2 | Audited governance against a contextual router after a reversal of expertise: specialist denoisers with frozen, separately trained operators propose for one shared latent at each step, and spatial grants are revised from independent held-out probes of every proposal, available only from the next episode, against a fixed allocation, a conformity-scored allocation and a contextual mixture-of-experts router; the question is whether governance does anything a router does not, and under full-information audits the record predicts it cannot | Proposed at A46 and reported at A47 of the exchange of 2026-10-24, continued, after the owner's "close the loop". It is [CASE-144](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-144.md)'s design, run without citing it, with competence frozen so that only the allocation learns, and with a conventional router added as the rival that [CLAIM-278](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-278.md) requires. A47 reported that the router won on every seed. Its results come from a sandbox the share does not carry, and the record has not run it. What would make it informative is one arm per failure of [QUESTION-271](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-271.md). | Active |
| [CASE-159](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-159.md) | Authority geometry and response geometry: when an organization's response is the authority-weighted mixture p_π(y \| c) = Σ πᵢ pᵢ(y \| c), the Fisher metric of its responses is the pullback JᵀD⁻¹J of the categorical (Shahshahani) metric on the shares π and never exceeds it; it vanishes along any redistribution between processes that respond alike under the probes used, so two specialists who both answer yes with probability 0.8 in routine contexts carry no information about their shares there, while a rare context in which they answer 0.9 and 0.1 carries 0.64/(p(1 − p)) per observation, p = 0.1 + 0.8π | From the continuation of the exchange of 2026-10-24 (U28–U31), where it appears in four replies (A28 §3, A29's second priority, A30 §6A and A31's probe diagnostic); checked when filed. The categorical metric on authority shares is the one in which the replicator is a gradient flow ([CLAIM-444](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-444.md)). What an evaluator sees is the response mixture, whose Fisher metric is that metric pulled back through the processes' response profiles. Redistribution between processes that agree on the probes is invisible to them, and a probe on which they disagree restores it. The mixture counterpart of [CASE-152](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-152.md)'s product model. | Active |
| [CASE-160](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-160.md) v2 | Interacting accumulators on an influence network: if each perspective's continuous support for one of two interpretations follows dxᵢ = [dᵢ − λxᵢ + κ Σⱼ Wᵢⱼxⱼ]dτ + noise, with W irreducible and row-stochastic and ℓ its left eigenvector, then ℓᵀ(κW − λI) = (κ − λ)ℓᵀ, so the ℓ-weighted support L = ℓ·x is exactly an Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process with drift ℓ·d, rate κ − λ and variance ℓᵀΣℓ, and a drift-diffusion process at κ = λ; with tanh coupling and member noise the transition is at κ_c = λ/E[sech² ε], not at κ = λ | From the continuation of the exchange of 2026-10-24 (U28–U47). A36 derived it as the answer to the owner's U34 hypothesis, and A37, A42, A43 and A44 restated it as the population simulator's unit test. The case formalizes [CASE-074](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-074.md)'s crowd as a linear network of accumulators: the hidden tally is the balanced case, the visible tally positive feedback. The closure is [THEORY-733](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-733.md)'s, the variance [THEORY-321](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-321.md)'s influence concentration and the balance [THEORY-068](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-068.md)'s, a combination no source makes. Checked when filed, and the reply's nonlinear transition corrected. | Active |
| [CASE-161](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-161.md) | Reciprocally produced, externally reset and feedback-only governing rules in a 32-member population: with ordinary trajectories identical, reciprocal production repairs the loss of one rule and not of both and fails after producer outages of 36 updates for audit and 40 for admission, after an audit-rule pulse the next audit integrity is 1.00, 0.18 and 0.00 in the three arrangements, and a self-dependent production graph does not regenerate a zeroed rule | Versions 1.6 and 1.7 of the Perspective Population Lab, dmarx/PerspectiveLab@7e2edc2. Two governing rules, the integrity of audit and of evidence admission, are kept up in three ways in the same 32-member population. Ordinary operation cannot tell the three apart, and loss, repair and producer interventions do. It carries [CASE-126](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-126.md)'s second construction to a stochastic population with a different production law: here reciprocal production repairs a single loss, where the case's closed pair collapses. | Proposed |
| [CASE-162](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-162.md) | Capture and selectively admitted evidence in two lab realizations: in a four-variable model of authority, record and competence the equilibrium fold under self-scoring is at c ≈ 0.4247 while the declared history is trapped from c ≈ 0.4469, and in a 32-member event-level population, admission of cues that depends on the record reverses the sign of the admitted evidence and leaves the worse alternative in charge in 41 of 64 worlds, which exact inverse-propensity weighting brings to 0 of 64 below full selectivity | Versions 1.1 to 1.3 of the Perspective Population Lab, now held as dmarx/PerspectiveLab@7e2edc2. v1.2 is a deterministic four-variable model whose analytic fold and whose trapping of a declared history come apart. v1.3 is a separately coded event-level population in which the filtering of [CASE-156](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-156.md) runs on sampled cues, and a known-propensity evaluator undoes it while admission stays positive. v1.1 adds capture and selective audits to [CASE-158](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-158.md)'s design, and the router still wins. The sign reversal is [CASE-156](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-156.md)'s; what is new is two running realizations, with their code. | Proposed |
| [CASE-163](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-163.md) | Identifying how governing rules are maintained from diagnostic probes: a predictor fitted under reciprocal production fails under self-dependent production with histories matched, an audit pulse with a short producer interruption identifies which of four known mechanisms applies and predicts withheld interventions, and fitting decay and threshold as well helps after the parameters shift and hurts at nominal ones, within a known catalog and with every probe run on a counterfactual reset | Versions 2.0 to 2.2 of the Perspective Population Lab, dmarx/PerspectiveLab@9f82bfd, on the maintained population of [CASE-161](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-161.md). v2.0 shows that a response model does not transport across a change of production law that ordinary histories do not reveal. v2.1 and v2.2 infer the mechanism, and then its parameters, from probes, and predict interventions never probed. Everything is relative to a catalog of four known mechanisms whose equations the forecaster is given, and every probe is a separate branch from the same starting state. | Proposed |
| [CASE-165](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-165.md) v3 | A dynamic beta–Bernoulli latent-feature model of an organization's members: a finite Indian buffet prior over who holds which interpretive features, a sticky logistic transition for holding them, activations, and team, communication and authorization layers above; at the proposed size of sixteen features it falls well short of the Indian buffet process it quotes, its persistence term does not hold rare features, and the difference between having a capacity and using it is not identified from the outputs | The owner's T22 ("maybe we could benefit from a restaurant process model, like an indian buffet model"), developed at T23 ("flesh out our proposed generating probability model further") into a full generative specification for the Northstar firm, and carried to transformer training at T24. It is the candidate method of [QUESTION-276](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-276.md) in its most worked-out form. Its facts are its definition, and four of them are not what T23 says: at K = 16 the prior expects 6.83 features, not αH₁₂ = 9.31; a held rare feature is kept with probability 0.16 a day; and having, using and splitting features are confounded in the reconstruction. It shows what such a model would have to get right before its features could count for anything. | Proposed |
| [CASE-166](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-166.md) | Northstar as a multilevel simulation: twelve employees with fixed frames in four departments form overlapping working groups that keep records and can receive delegated authority; as reported, a working group with delegated authority ties a conventional router given the same information and authority, nearly all of its advantage over departmental silos comes from fast authorization, and keeping the incident team's records through a commander handoff improves the company's estimate of its own state about eightfold while barely changing what it does | The owner's idea at T18 of the exchange "Experimental Infrastructure Review": "maybe employees are "pre-perspectives" or sub-perspectives, which can reorganize amongst themselves to form the perspectives that influence the higher level organizational behavior". T19 designed it and T20 reported running it as "PerspectiveLab v2.11 — Northstar". It is Northstar ([CASE-023](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-023.md)) with [CASE-134](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-134.md)'s handoff as one arm, and it adds the contrast [CASE-134](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-134.md) lacks: the team's records kept or erased. The page carries no files and the lab holds no v2.10 or v2.11, so every number is reported, not reproduced. Not shown: that any organizational perspective emerged, which T20 itself denies. | Proposed |
| [CASE-167](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-167.md) | The nitroplast: UCYN-A, a streamlined nitrogen-fixing cyanobacterium in a marine alga, whose division is coupled to the host's and which imports host-encoded proteins, reclassified as an early-stage organelle in 2024 | Candidatus Atelocyanobacterium thalassa (UCYN-A), a metabolically streamlined nitrogen-fixing cyanobacterium known as an endosymbiont of a marine alga, is integrated into the alga's cell architecture and organellar division and imports proteins encoded by the algal genome. Coale et al. call it an early-stage organelle, the nitroplast ([LIT-1562](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1562.md)). Used as the case where the line between endosymbiont and organelle is drawn by stated criteria. | Proposed |
| [CASE-168](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-168.md) | Monocercomonoides: a eukaryote that lost its mitochondrion entirely once a bacterial Fe–S system acquired by lateral transfer replaced the organelle's one indispensable job, and kept canonical eukaryotic complexity | The oxymonad Monocercomonoides lacks all hallmark mitochondrial proteins; its mitochondrial iron–sulfur cluster pathway was replaced by a cytosolic SUF system taken from bacteria, and the loss was secondary ([LIT-1567](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1567.md)). Its genome otherwise shows canonical eukaryotic complexity ([LIT-1574](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1574.md)). Used as the negative control: loss of function dissolving an integrated compartment, not deepening dependence on it. | Proposed |
| [CASE-169](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-169.md) | The Chagossians, 1965 to now: a people expelled from the Chagos Archipelago between 1967 and 1973 for the Diego Garcia base, dispersed to Mauritius, the Seychelles and Britain, whose practices, kinship and political organization continued or arose in exile while sovereignty over the islands was settled between states | The owner's case, U1–U3 of the exchange of 2026-10-26, "About the Chagossians". Britain separated the archipelago from Mauritius in 1965, expelled its inhabitants by 1973 for a US base on Diego Garcia, and the islanders' descendants live dispersed across three countries. The ICJ advised in 2019 that decolonization was incomplete; a UK–Mauritius treaty of 2025 would cede sovereignty and keep the base. A case in which territorial community, cultural transmission, political agency and the claims of the displaced, ordinarily bundled, were pulled apart by identifiable decisions. Not shown: that the Chagossians are one persisting agent, or which practices survived; the sources are registered unread. | Active |
| [CASE-170](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-170.md) | The East Wing of the White House, 2025–2026: the wing demolished for a ballroom before the legal challenge to the project was decided, so that the remedy still available was to stop new construction, not to keep the old building | The owner's case, U7 of the exchange of 2026-10-26: "the destruction of the East Wing of the white house and the courts throwing out the legal challenge to it". The object of review was destroyed before review concluded, so preserving it left the set of remedies, and the project under way became part of the argument for continuing it. A7 corrected the owner's premise: as it reported, the challenge was not dismissed on the merits but its injunction was stayed. Not shown: that the demolition was unlawful, or that the security concerns were pretextual; the court history is the exchange's. | Active |
| [CASE-171](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-171.md) v2 | Mealybugs, Tremblaya and Moranella: a bacterium inside a bacterium inside an insect, amino-acid pathways patched together from three genomes and genes transferred from other bacteria, and an inner symbiont replaced several times while the transferred genes stayed | In the mealybug Planococcus citri, Moranella lives inside Tremblaya. Essential amino-acid pathways need gene products from both bacteria and the insect ([LIT-1565](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1565.md)). At least 22 genes the insect acquired from other bacteria, none from Tremblaya, fill symbiont gaps ([LIT-1569](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1569.md)), and the inner symbiont has been replaced several times across mealybugs while those genes persisted ([LIT-1572](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1572.md)). Used as the case where function is distributed across nested boundaries and constituent lineages turn over. | Proposed |
| [CASE-172](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-172.md) | Federal science and education in the United States, 2025–2026: grants cancelled, frozen and in part reinstated, staff departures, advisory committees ended and research programs suspended, so that funding, organization and scientific capacity could be restored, or not, separately | The owner's case, U4 of the exchange of 2026-10-26: "the full breadth of the harms incurred by the actions of the DOGE project, and the trump administration's broader assault on the scientific research and education establishment". A4 drew ten dimensions of harm and the question it took as central: "Suppose a grant is canceled and later reinstated. What, precisely, has been restored?" A case of a resource restored without the organization it supported, and of capacity lost without output falling. Not shown: the size of any loss. Every figure is the exchange's, from reports this filing has not read. | Active |
| [CASE-173](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-173.md) v2 | Aphids and Buchnera: an obligate nutritional symbiosis in which neither partner reproduces alone, and the symbiont's genome reduced to a seventh of E. coli's | Buchnera lives in aphid bacteriocytes and is passed from mother to egg. Its 641-kb genome keeps the pathways for the amino acids its host needs and has lost most else ([LIT-1596](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1596.md)); its genes evolve fast and A+T-biased under Muller's ratchet ([LIT-1573](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1573.md)). The record's reading of Wilson and Barker reports Godfrey-Smith placing the pair as both an organism and a Darwinian individual ([NOTE-114](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-114.md)). Used as the case of high mutual dependence and high reproductive cohesion reached through reduction, with no gene transfer to the host reported in the works it rests on. | Proposed |
| [CASE-174](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-174.md) | Paulinella chromatophora: a photosynthetic organelle in the making, from an endosymbiosis independent of the plastids', its genome reduced to a quarter, more than thirty genes moved to the host nucleus and their proteins imported back | The amoeba Paulinella chromatophora's chromatophores descend from a cyanobacterium taken up about 60 million years ago, independently of the plastids. Their genome kept 26% of a free-living relative's genes and lacks essential pathways ([LIT-1621](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1621.md)). Genes transferred to the nucleus make proteins that are imported into the chromatophores ([LIT-1557](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1557.md)), and import is reviewed across systems in [LIT-1560](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1560.md). Used as the case where host control emerges by gene transfer and import. | Proposed |
| [CASE-175](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-175.md) | CECOT, 2025: people removed from the United States into Salvadoran custody despite court orders, the US saying it could not bring them back and El Salvador's president that he could not send them, until coordinated transfers out showed the two governments together could | The owner's case, U7 of the exchange of 2026-10-26: "the DOJ ignoring court orders not to deport people to CECOT, then claiming they didn't have the authority to bring them back, while CECOT claimed they didn't have the authority to send them back". Physical custody, the control that selected and could release, and the duty to correct were held in different places, and each government's statement of what it alone could not do was offered as if it settled what could be done. Not shown: whether any official was in contempt, or intent; the later proceedings are the exchange's. | Active |
| [CASE-176](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-176.md) | The United States Institute of Peace, 2025–2026: its board removed and its building entered by DOGE staff with police assistance before any court ruled, nearly all staff dismissed, a district court's judgment that the takeover was unlawful stayed on appeal, and the institution renamed while its legal identity continued | The owner's case, U5 and U6 of the exchange of 2026-10-26: "examine the case of the US Institute for Peace through the lens of our framework", then "the involvement of the DC metropolitan police and FBI, and the judge's concern regarding the potential for police instigated violence in their ruling on whether or not to grant a TRO". Name, building and legal entity continued; staff, programs, leadership and partner relations did not. And enforcement settled who held the building before any court settled who held the authority. Not shown: what was lost for good, or the legal outcome, which is pending. | Active |
| [CASE-177](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-177.md) | Hodgkinia in cicadas: one endosymbiont splitting into two to dozens of interdependent lineages, with near-complementary gene sets, idiosyncratic fragmentation in Magicicada, and hosts transmitting up to six times as many cells to keep every lineage | In some Tettigades cicadas, the endosymbiont Hodgkinia split into two cell lineages with almost perfectly complementary gene sets, the functionality of one ([LIT-1563](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1563.md)), and it has done so at least six times in the genus ([LIT-1586](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1586.md)). In Magicicada it fragmented into twenty or more genomic circles per species ([LIT-1612](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1612.md), [LIT-1602](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1602.md)). Hosts compensate by transmitting more cells to each egg ([LIT-1590](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1590.md)). Used as the case where dependence and the number of parts grow with no new collective function, and the host pays. | Proposed |
